title: Docker: build, run and diagnose
prerequisites: A terminal, Docker and a local checkout
summary: Read the actual Dockerfile, observe build caching, run Makan and diagnose a failed port mapping.

title: Git: ship a change you can undo
summary: Make a focused branch, inspect a diff, resolve a conflict and revert a change without rewriting shared history.

title: Cilium, Flannel and NetworkPolicy
prerequisites: kubectl, a disposable cluster with a policy-capable CNI
summary: Separate networking from ingress, test isolation and restore only the traffic your service needs.

title: AWS networking: trace the packet, prove the route
prerequisites: Linux routing and DNS; AWS CLI v2; a disposable AWS account with VPC permissions.
summary: Build a private network boundary, explain NAT versus IGW, and diagnose SG, NACL and return-path failures.

quiz.question: Which change alone makes an EC2 instance internet reachable?
choices: An IGW attached to its VPC
None: address, route and controls must all align
quiz.explanation: An IGW attachment alone supplies neither a subnet route nor a public IPv4 association.

quiz.question: Which rule set needs explicit return ephemeral-port rules?
quiz.explanation: NACLs evaluate each direction independently.

encouragement.beforeLab: Trace one connection at a time. Once the packet path makes sense, the service names become easier to remember.
encouragement.afterValidation: You have a route to follow now. Treat the next failed connection as evidence, not a reason to start over.

title: AWS identity: roles, STS and secret boundaries
prerequisites: AWS 01; sandbox IAM role-management permissions; AWS CLI v2 and jq.
summary: Separate trust from permissions, evaluate least privilege, and retrieve secrets through a workload role rather than embedded credentials.

quiz.question: AssumeRole succeeds but GetSecretValue fails. Which boundary passed?
quiz.explanation: Obtaining a session does not grant every service action.

quiz.question: Does Terraform sensitive=true remove a password from state?
quiz.explanation: Sensitive controls presentation; state and plan access still need protection.

encouragement.beforeLab: Start with one identity, one action and one resource. Clear boundaries beat a policy full of guesses.
encouragement.afterValidation: A denied request can be a successful security test. Explain which boundary held before changing it.

title: AWS compute: ALB health, launch templates and recovery
prerequisites: AWS 01–02; Terraform CLI; optional learner-deployed capstone for runtime drills.
summary: Operate EC2 behind an ALB, distinguish probe success from readiness, and diagnose Auto Scaling replacement loops.

quiz.question: A DB outage makes every deep probe fail. Should EC2 replacement be the primary repair?
choices: No, isolate the shared dependency failure
quiz.explanation: Replacing healthy processes does not restore a shared database and can amplify disruption.

quiz.question: Does a new launch-template version update all existing instances automatically?
choices: No; use a controlled replacement/refresh strategy
quiz.explanation: Templates define future launches. Existing instances need an explicit rollout.

encouragement.beforeLab: Make the smallest failure you can observe. A short, clear recovery timeline teaches more than a large uncontrolled outage.
encouragement.afterValidation: Keep the evidence from your recovery drill. You are building an explanation you can reproduce, not just a working screenshot.

title: AWS data: RDS, S3, recovery and cost tradeoffs
prerequisites: AWS 01–03; AWS CLI; optional capstone RDS and a learner-owned S3 test bucket.
summary: Distinguish availability from recovery, test versioned object restoration, and design measurable RPO/RTO for WordPress.

quiz.question: What protects against an application deleting valid rows?
choices: Tested backups/PITR with a cutover runbook
quiz.explanation: Availability replicas do not preserve independent historical application state.

quiz.question: Does deleting current objects empty a versioned bucket completely?
choices: No, retained versions and markers remain
quiz.explanation: Old versions and delete markers must also be considered.

encouragement.beforeLab: Recovery is a skill you can practise. Begin with one harmless object and prove that the original bytes come back.
encouragement.afterValidation: A tested restore is worth keeping in your notes. Be clear about what you recovered and what still needs a rehearsal.

title: AWS Terraform: modules, state, drift and lifecycle
prerequisites: AWS networking and IAM; Terraform 1.10+; sandbox state bucket provisioned separately.
summary: Review reusable boundaries, migrate state safely, detect drift without applying, and understand destructive lifecycle changes.

quiz.question: What does plan -refresh-only propose?
choices: Restoring every remote object to code
Updating recorded state to observed reality
quiz.explanation: Refresh-only proposes state updates; a normal plan proposes infrastructure reconciliation.

quiz.question: Which detailed-exitcode indicates a successful plan with changes?
quiz.explanation: 0 means no changes, 1 error, 2 successful with differences.

encouragement.beforeLab: Slow down at the plan. Understanding one proposed change is progress, even when the right decision is not to apply it.
encouragement.afterValidation: You do not need to fix drift blindly. Classify the change, choose the owner and make the next action deliberate.

title: AWS delivery: GitHub OIDC and reviewed Terraform plans
prerequisites: AWS 02 and 05; a separate sandbox GitHub repository; permission to create a scoped federated role.
summary: Replace static CI keys with scoped federation and design a reviewed deployment boundary that untrusted pull requests cannot cross.

quiz.question: A job uses a GitHub environment. Which subject must trust match?
quiz.explanation: Environment jobs carry an environment subject; protection rules must also be configured.

quiz.question: What should an untrusted PR receive?
choices: Credential-free checks, not privileged Terraform execution
quiz.explanation: Untrusted Terraform/provider code must not run with deployment credentials.

encouragement.beforeLab: Follow the identity exchange step by step. A narrow trust rule is easier to defend than a convenient wildcard.
encouragement.afterValidation: A pipeline refusing the wrong identity is doing its job. Keep that failed test alongside the successful run.

title: AWS capstone: a secure, highly available WordPress service
prerequisites: AWS 01–06; Terraform 1.10+; dedicated account; approved budget; existing ACM certificate and matching DNS name.
summary: Deploy and defend two-AZ WordPress with private EC2, ALB TLS, shared EFS, Multi-AZ RDS and role-based secrets; prove failure recovery and tear it down.

quiz.question: What makes uploads survive app-instance replacement?
choices: A shared durable filesystem plus a separate backup strategy
quiz.explanation: Shared EFS keeps uploads visible across instances; backups address historical recovery.

quiz.question: Does a green shallow probe prove historical restore or credential rotation works?
quiz.explanation: Each health/recovery claim needs its own evidence.

encouragement.beforeLab: Bring the pieces together one boundary at a time. Review the plan, prove the path, then test a small failure.
encouragement.afterValidation: You have reached the integration stage. An honest record of what worked, failed and remains untested makes this project stronger.

title: Azure operating model: subscriptions, Entra ID and RBAC
prerequisites: Linux, networking and Git basics; Azure CLI; a dedicated sandbox subscription and permission to create a lab Resource Group.
summary: Establish tenant/subscription scope, separate management and data-plane rights, and diagnose effective Azure authorization.

quiz.question: Is a Resource Group a network isolation boundary?
choices: No; routing and network controls determine reachability
quiz.explanation: RGs organize management and lifecycle; they do not create network isolation.

quiz.question: Does Contributor always grant blob reads using Entra authentication?
choices: No; data-plane authorization must be checked
quiz.explanation: Management actions and dataActions are separate.

encouragement.beforeLab: A new cloud does not erase your existing skills. Start by mapping the scopes and identities, then test one permission.
encouragement.afterValidation: Keep your scope diagram nearby. The next modules will give those boundaries a network and an application.

title: Azure networking: NSGs, routes, private endpoints and DNS
prerequisites: Azure 01; Azure CLI; sandbox VNet rights; basic TCP and DNS diagnosis.
summary: Trace effective routes and NSGs, distinguish private endpoints from service endpoints, and diagnose private DNS from the workload.

quiz.question: A private endpoint exists. Is public access necessarily disabled?
choices: No, configure the service public-access setting separately
quiz.explanation: Creating a private endpoint does not automatically close the public service endpoint.

quiz.question: Where should you test DNS for a private workload?
choices: Inside the workload network using its resolver
quiz.explanation: Private zone links and resolver paths determine the workload view.

encouragement.beforeLab: Use familiar troubleshooting habits: resolve the name, follow the route and check the rule that actually applies.
encouragement.afterValidation: If the first lookup fails, you have a starting point. Change one layer at a time and compare the result.

title: Azure compute: VMs, scale sets and load-balancing choices
prerequisites: Azure 01–02; Azure CLI; optional Azure 07 capstone for private VM runtime inspection.
summary: Choose L4 versus L7 ingress, inspect private VM health and explain VMSS rollout, probes and availability choices.

quiz.question: Which service directly fits host/path-based HTTP routing and WAF?
quiz.explanation: Application Gateway provides L7 HTTP routing and WAF options.

quiz.question: Does one running VM prove application high availability?
quiz.explanation: Process readiness and independent failure domains need separate validation.

encouragement.beforeLab: Start with a listener you can test. Build confidence in the private path before adding another scaling or routing layer.
encouragement.afterValidation: A running VM and a ready application are different achievements. Your evidence should make the difference clear.

title: Azure services: Storage, Key Vault, identities and Monitor
prerequisites: Azure 01–03; optional deployed Azure capstone; data-role assignment rights for extensions.
summary: Trace VM managed identity to private Blob access, distinguish Key Vault network and role failures, and collect useful operating signals.

quiz.question: Does a managed identity token itself grant Blob access?
choices: No; the data role and network path must also permit it
quiz.explanation: Authentication, authorization and connectivity are distinct.

quiz.question: Which signal records Azure control-plane changes?
quiz.explanation: Activity Log records control-plane operations; guest logs need an ingestion path.

encouragement.beforeLab: Take the token, role and network checks separately. You do not have to solve every layer at once.
encouragement.afterValidation: Keep one successful check and one useful failure. Together they show that you understand the access boundary.

title: Azure Terraform: provider identity and Blob remote state
prerequisites: Azure 01–04; Terraform 1.10+; separate sandbox state Storage Account/container.
summary: Separate provider and backend authentication, use Entra-authorized state, and recover safely from drift and orphaned Blob leases.

quiz.question: Which component locks Azure Blob state?
choices: The backend using a Blob lease
quiz.explanation: The AzureRM backend uses native Blob locking/consistency capabilities.

quiz.question: Should the workload destroy also delete its own backend?
quiz.explanation: Independent backend lifecycle preserves the state and recovery boundary.

encouragement.beforeLab: Keep the backend and provider paths separate in your notes. Two clear diagrams are better than one confusing error.
encouragement.afterValidation: A reviewed no-change plan is useful evidence too. Predictability is part of operating infrastructure well.

title: Azure delivery: federated GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines
prerequisites: Azure 01 and 05; separate sandbox repo/project; Entra application/identity and federated-credential administration.
summary: Configure workload federation in both CI systems, protect service connections, and separate preview from approved apply.

quiz.question: Can you reuse GitHub issuer/subject values unchanged for Azure DevOps?
choices: No; trust the actual service-connection claims
quiz.explanation: The CI systems have distinct federation issuers/subjects.

quiz.question: Where should an independently administered deployment gate live?
quiz.explanation: External checks prevent a pipeline edit from removing its own approval boundary.

encouragement.beforeLab: Work through one CI system first. Once its trust boundary is clear, compare the other system deliberately.
encouragement.afterValidation: Protecting the path matters as much as making it run. Keep the denied identity test in your evidence.

title: Azure capstone: build and diagnose a private application
prerequisites: Azure 01–06; Terraform 1.10+; sandbox budget and quotas; SSH public key; Azure CLI.
summary: Build a private VM application behind an internal load balancer, authorize private Blob access through managed identity, and diagnose DNS, process and RBAC failures.

quiz.question: Does localhost curl prove the internal load balancer client path?
choices: No, test the VIP from a separate allowed client
quiz.explanation: The backend listener and client-to-VIP path are different checks.

quiz.question: What does an IMDS token followed by a Storage 403 suggest?
choices: Inspect data authorization and network policy independently
quiz.explanation: Authentication can succeed while data access or network restrictions deny the request.

encouragement.beforeLab: You do not need a perfect first deployment. Work through the validation checks and let each result guide the next step.
encouragement.afterValidation: Finish with a clear incident story and verified cleanup. Knowing the limits of your build is part of knowing the build.
